newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin heart surgery may be delayed, surgeon says.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin heart surgery may be delayed, surgeon says.

text.p: A Russian surgeon chosen to carry out heart surery on President Boris Yeltsin said in a television interview shown on Sunday that the operation could be delayed by up to two months because of the patient's condition.

Renat Akchurin told NTV commercial television that Yeltsin, 65, would not accept the idea of cancelling the bypass surgery aimed at improving the blood supply to his heart because it would dramatically limit his physical activities.
Asked by Yevgeny Kiselyov, anchorman of the weekly show Itogi, when the operation might take place, Akchurin answered: "Within 1-1/2 or two months."
Akchurin, in unusually open remarks, told Reuters on Saturday it might be too dangerous to go ahead with the planned bypass surgery, but added he hoped it would still be possible.
He told Itogi a committee of Russian and foreign doctors was due to decide on Wednesday or Thursday when to hold an operation and whether it was generally safe for the patient.
"We will see how the patient is prepared for the operation," Akchurin said. "Any risk should be justified. If the risk is justified go and do the operation. If it is not, don't do silly things."
Asked whether the operation could be cancelled for good, Akchurin answered: "It is possible but special conditions should be created for the president then."
"We would be forced to limit his physical activies. He is not going to tolerate that."
Yeltsin disapeared from the public eye in late June, right in the middle of his vigorous re-election campaign for a second term in the Kremlin.

Yeltsin aides insisted before and after his July 3 victory that the president, who has a history of heart problems, was all right, just overtired. Yeltsin took a vacation at the Zavidovo residence outside Moscow and later at a hunting lodge.

Earlier this month Yeltsin disclosed in a televised interview that said he needed heart surgery and that he had agreed to undergo it. Yeltsin said the operation was likely to take place in late September.
Akchurin appeared quite critical about the way Yeltsin was handled while in Zavidovo.
"I saw Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) two or three weeks ago," he said. "We have looked at results of his Zavidovo period."
"I cannot say I was too pleased with these results. He was tiring himself, hunting, fishing. This is not something we can recommend for this sort of patient."
Akchurin said that apart from that Yeltsin, who is in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital, was quite optimistic and was insistent in his commitment to undergo surgery.
He made clear he was not in favour of an early operation.
"We need to go through a certain preparatory period and Boris Nikolayvich, who whips us up all the time, seems to understand this," Akchurin said.
"An earlier date for the operation means bigger risks," he added. "We undertake to perform an operation but with minimum risks."
Akchurin said he will head a team of 12 surgeons if the operation takes place.
He said that he had carried out bypass surgery on Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin eight years ago.
